html:
Enrico Dandolo was doge of Venice from 1192 to 1205, best known for steering the Fourth Crusade to Constantinople. He was elected doge when he was already in his eighties, and he was blind or nearly so.

Before that he had served as a diplomat, including missions to Constantinople in the years after the arrest of the Venetians in 1171. Later stories said the Byzantines blinded him then, but the cause of his blindness is unknown.

In 1201 Venice agreed to build a fleet for the crusaders, who then could not pay for it. Dandolo had them work off the debt by taking Zara, a Christian city on the Adriatic, in the siege of Zara of 1202. Then the crusade took up the cause of the Byzantine prince Alexios Angelos and sailed for Constantinople. Dandolo, in armour, led the Venetian attack from the bow of his galley in the siege of 1203, and the city was sacked in 1204.

Venice won a large share of the empire's lands and ports, the base of its colonial empire. Dandolo died in Constantinople in 1205 and was buried in Hagia Sophia.
